summary: A type whose copies equal their original and change independently of it, so values can be copied, assigned and compared like integers.
definition: A type whose copy, assignment and equality behave as they do for `int`: a copy compares equal to its original, and changing one never affects the other. Sparkles requires it of events and identifiers so tests can compare and replay them; see [local reasoning](/research/sean-parent/local-reasoning).

authority.text: Sean Parent: contracts and regular types

summary: A design in which a protocol or state machine performs no I/O itself: the caller supplies bytes, time and events, and performs the actions it returns.
definition: A protocol or state-machine implementation that never reads, writes, sleeps or consults a clock. Its caller feeds it input and carries out the effects it requests, which makes the core deterministic and testable without sockets or timers. [Writing Specification Docs](/guidelines/spec-docs) asks for this separation wherever the domain permits.

summary: The decision whether a candidate matches a fuzzy query at all, made separately from how highly it ranks.
definition: In `sparkles:fuzzy`, a query part admits a candidate when the part, after deleting at most its typo budget of characters, occurs in order within the candidate. Admission alone decides which candidates match and what is highlighted; ranking only orders the admitted ones.

summary: The one deterministically chosen set of candidate characters that proves a fuzzy match and is highlighted to the user.
definition: Of all the ways an admitted query part can be found in a candidate, the one with the fewest deleted query characters, then the earliest final character, then the earliest positions. It supplies both the highlighted ranges and the window the ranking score is computed over.

summary: One font inside a font file: the whole file for a single-font file, or one member of a collection, identified by the file's bytes and an index.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, one font inside a byte buffer, read in place and never changed after it opens. A single-font file holds one face; an [OpenType collection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/otff#font-collections) holds several, picked by index.

summary: A face at a particular size, with one fixed set of variable-font coordinates and any faked styling, from which every glyph, metric and shaping result is derived.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, a copyable value combining a [face](/glossary#face), a size in pixels per em, one vector of [normalized variation coordinates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/otvaroverview#coordinate-scales-and-normalization) and a [synthesis](/glossary#synthesis). It is the only place variation coordinates are stored, so shaping, metrics, outlines and rasterization all read the same ones. Not to be confused with an OpenType *named* instance.

summary: What font matching had to fake to approximate a requested style: an emboldening amount, a slant, or a variation-axis setting.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the value a match returns alongside the chosen face, saying how to approximate what the face lacks: embolden by an amount, skew by an angle, or set an axis. Shaping and rasterization both consume it, so faked bold and italic look the same everywhere.

summary: The fixed box a terminal lays characters out in, with its baseline, underline and strikeout positions, in whole device pixels.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the cell width and height, baseline, and underline and strikeout positions and thicknesses derived from a face at a size, rounded to whole device pixels by one documented rule. The cell width is the advance of the digit zero.

summary: A value that fully determines one rendered glyph, so equal keys always produce identical pixels and caches can be keyed by it.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the face identity, glyph, size, variation coordinates, subpixel offset and render flags of one rasterization. Equal keys produce byte-identical output, which is what makes glyph caches separate values instead of state inside a face.

summary: Somewhere fonts come from: explicit files, a directory, the bundled fonts, or the system's list of installed fonts.
definition: An input to the [font catalog](/glossary#font-catalog): explicit files, a directory, the font directory Sparkles bundles, or the files the platform lists as installed. A platform source only lists files; the library's own parser describes them.

summary: What the font catalog stores about one face: enough to match it and to test which characters it covers without opening it.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the catalog's description of one [face](/glossary#face): names, style, width, weight, spacing and character coverage, read by the library's own parser and cached on disk against the file's size and modification time.

summary: The index of known fonts built from every font source, over which matching and fallback run identically on every platform.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the set of [face records](/glossary#face-record) built from all [font sources](/glossary#font-source). Platforms differ only in which files they list; matching and fallback rules over the catalog are the same everywhere. Distinct from a collection index, which picks a face inside one file.

summary: The ordered list of fonts consulted, character by character, when the preferred font cannot draw a character.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, an ordered list of [face records](/glossary#face-record) beginning with the matched face and keeping only faces that add character coverage. A face opens on first use, and each character's answer is remembered.

summary: Used alone, the fraction of each pixel a glyph's shape covers, which a rasterizer produces; which characters a font maps is called character coverage.
definition: In `sparkles:font`, the 8-bit per-pixel value a rasterizer writes for a glyph: 0 where the outline leaves the pixel empty, 255 where it covers it. The set of characters a face maps through its `cmap` table is called *character coverage*.

summary: A rendered sample of a font: preview text, a waterfall of sizes, a code sample, a glyph map or a comparison, shown as one image.
definition: In the font explorer, a block of sample text or glyphs rendered in the font being examined. Every specimen is one bitmap the font library rasterizes, shown as an image in a window or over the kitty graphics protocol in a terminal, never drawn in the terminal's own font.

summary: One of three layouts the font explorer chooses from its width in interface cells: wide, medium or narrow.
definition: In the font explorer, the layout chosen by width measured in interface cells, so one rule serves a window and a terminal: *wide* at 150 cells or more shows every pane, *medium* folds the sources into the family list, and *narrow* below 100 shows only the specimens with the other panes as overlays.

summary: A check that lists every glyph whose width differs from a terminal cell and every ligature that changes the number of glyphs.
definition: In the font explorer, the check that tells whether a programming font keeps a terminal's character grid: glyphs whose advance differs from the face's [cell metrics](/glossary#cell-metrics), and ligatures that change the glyph count, each with the characters involved.

summary: A statically typed record of handler values, one per service such as the clock, the network or processes, passed to code instead of letting it reach those services directly.
definition: In `sparkles:event-horizon`, a `Ctx` struct holding one handler per uniquely labeled capability; a function that needs several services takes a row, one that needs one takes it bare. Swapping a handler means passing a value of a different type, so tests substitute virtual time or a simulated network with no run-time dispatch. It is a testability and least-authority convention, not a security boundary.

summary: In sparkles:versions, a type that is both a version value of one package ecosystem and the handle that parses that ecosystem's version strings.
definition: A plain struct that is at once the version value for one ecosystem (SemVer, PEP 440, Debian, …) and the handle carrying its parser and Package URL type. It satisfies the version concept, a total order plus text rendering, and the scheme concept; every further capability is optional and detected at compile time.

summary: The span of a workload test's body, run once or a few times, across which the test runner reports how every measurement source changed.
definition: A `@workload` test is measured as a window rather than per iteration: each source is read once at the window's opening and closing edges, and the runner reports the deltas, including a split of elapsed time into on-CPU and off-CPU components. The body is never re-run for counting.

summary: Whether a measured metric barely perturbs the work, and so may back a reported result, or only helps explain one.
definition: Every metric in the test runner's catalog is either _quantitative_, with near-zero perturbation and the only class a reported or gated number may read, or _diagnostic_, which perturbs the measurement and is rendered separately, never blended into a headline.

summary: A capability a measurement source cannot provide on this host, reported by name with its reason instead of failing the run or printing a number.
definition: Each measurement source opens through a run-time probe and reports what it can measure. A missing capability is recorded as an absence with a human-readable reason; its columns are omitted or render as unavailable, never as zero or an unlabeled estimate.

summary: A named visual role, such as error text or a selected row, that a widget refers to instead of a concrete color.
definition: In `sparkles:ui`, a widget names a slot rather than a color or style; the theme's palette resolves each slot to a concrete appearance (colors, attributes, border, font role) while the display list is built, so one theme restyles every target.

summary: The integer unit of space in which the UI toolkit lays out every widget: one character position on a terminal, and a backend-chosen size elsewhere.
definition: Every coordinate and extent in `sparkles:ui` layout is a whole number of cells; no floating-point value enters layout. Mapping cells to pixels or CSS lengths is the canvas's job, so pixel backends may still position content more finely.

summary: The flat sequence of drawing operations the UI toolkit produces from a laid-out widget tree, with every visual role already resolved.
definition: In `sparkles:ui`, the display list is the last backend-neutral stage: each operation carries its slot, its resolved appearance and its clip state, so a backend paints it without consulting the theme or the widget tree. Tests inspect it through a recording canvas.

summary: The category hue assigns to a loaded document, such as highlighted source, markdown, a delimiter-separated table, a diff or an annotated code sample, which decides how it is viewed.
definition: The category a document gets when hue loads a target, chosen from its content rather than from a command-line mode. Each kind produces one `sparkles:ui` widget tree that every backend paints, and kinds compose: a markdown document may embed a code block of another kind.

summary: The level of interactivity a viewer requirement needs: static output, a live event loop, or positions finer than a terminal cell.
definition: A classification of hue's viewer requirements by what they need from a backend, not by which backend paints them: `passive` (static output), `interactive` (a live event loop) and `precise` (sub-cell positions or continuous time). Where a backend cannot reach a tier, the requirement states the degradation; any other difference between backends is a defect.

summary: The logical tree of files, directories and symbolic links that a package will contain, described independently of any host filesystem and validated before anything is written.
definition: The format-neutral input to `sparkles:packaging`: an ordered tree of regular files, directories and symbolic links with logical `/`-separated paths and honest metadata. Every artifact format is produced from it, and its paths are validated before any host path is joined.

summary: A canonical, versioned JSON record, written last by a packaging run, of the final bytes and digests of every artifact it produced and how each was made.
definition: The machine-readable output of a successful `sparkles:packaging` run for one target: resolved identity, stage inventory, final artifact sizes and SHA-256 digests, encoder or tool versions, and signing status. It is evidence for later publishing tools, not an SBOM or a provenance attestation.

summary: The tree of commands and subcommands that a command-line parser derives at compile time from a root command type and the command types nested in or registered into it.
definition: In `sparkles:core-cli`, the compile-time tree of a CLI's commands. A command's children are its nested `@(Command)` structs and the types it registers with `mixin addSubCommand`, in compiler member order, or the variants of an explicit `@Subcommands` field when it has one.

authority.text: core-cli args specification: The command graph
core-cli args specification: Command child discovery

summary: A command-line command that has subcommands of its own, such as worktree in git worktree list.
definition: In `sparkles:core-cli`, a command with at least one child in the [command graph](/glossary#command-graph). Its parse-tree node holds the selected child's node, and selecting the group without naming a child is an incorrect call unless the group declares default handling.

authority.text: core-cli args specification: Default handlers for command groups

summary: One named design decision with a value, such as a color, a length, a glyph choice or a font role, addressed by a dotted path like text.primary.
definition: In the Sparkles design system every token sits on one of three tiers: a *primitive* holds a raw value, a *semantic* token names a role, and a *component* token names a part of one component; each tier aliases the one below, and the alias graph must be acyclic. A theme assigns values to tokens.

summary: A condition of a widget, such as hover, focused, selected, pressed or disabled, that can change how its visual roles are drawn.
definition: Slot resolution in `sparkles:ui` takes the set of active interaction states as a second argument. A theme overrides a state sparsely; where no active state has an override the resting appearance is used, and among several active states the highest-precedence override wins.

summary: The defined rule by which a rendering target that cannot draw a design value exactly, such as a pixel corner radius on a character grid, renders it anyway.
definition: In the Sparkles design system a metric finer than a [cell](/glossary#cell) is typed in device pixels and carries a projection onto cell targets; each target declares per metric whether it honours or projects it, so no value is silently dropped. Glyphs and borders are projected the same way.

summary: A dotted address, such as key.action, that names one field reachable from a queried D type in a DQL query.
definition: A dotted address that names one field, getter or index reachable from a queried D type, such as `pointer.logicalPosition.x`. The alternatives of a `SumType` field are transparent: their fields join the path of the field that holds the union, so `key.action` reads the keyboard alternative's action.

summary: The table of every path a D type offers to DQL queries, generated from the type at compile time and used to validate queries and print help.
definition: The table of every [DQL path](/glossary#dql-path) a D type offers, with each path's type, category and documentation, generated at compile time through the [reflection kernel](/libs/reflection/). The parser rejects a query naming a path outside it, and the help protocol prints it.

summary: The release tool's mode that cuts an unreleased backlog into a chain of consecutive releases, each with its own version and notes, at boundaries proposed by an AI agent and validated by the tool.
definition: The `release --split` mode of `sparkles:release`. It matches commits to the pull requests that introduced them, groups them into [pull-request-atomic units](/glossary#pr-atomic-unit), asks a command-line agent for release boundaries and themes, validates and approves the plan, and tags each slice oldest first. Its counterpart, classic mode, makes a single release.

summary: A contiguous run of commits that the release tool never divides between two releases: one merged pull request with all its commits, or a single commit pushed directly.
definition: The indivisible element of a [split mode](/glossary#split-mode) backlog. A unit ends at the first commit where every pull request opened so far has closed, so interleaved pull requests merge into one wider unit; release boundaries fall only between units.

summary: The ordered, balanced sequence of enter-label, leave-label and source-range events over byte offsets that every syntax-highlighting engine emits and every renderer folds.
definition: The single seam of `sparkles:syntax`: engines emit `source(start, end)`, `push(label)` and `pop` events in position order with every push matched by a pop, and renderers fold that sequence into ANSI, HTML or styled runs. The stream is infallible; engine failures surface before it, never inside it. The event model follows tree-sitter's reference highlighter.

summary: A hierarchical dotted name, such as keyword.control, that a syntax-highlighting engine assigns to a span of source text and a theme maps to a style.
definition: A name from the canonical, TextMate-scope-compatible vocabulary of `sparkles:syntax`, interned to a numeric id at configure time. Themes and capture names both resolve by longest dotted prefix, so `keyword.control.import` falls back to `keyword.control` and then `keyword`; capture names additionally consult an alias table that reconciles other grammar dialects.

summary: The rule that a syntax highlighter never rejects its input: the worst legal output is the source text uncolored.
definition: Unlike a parser, a highlighter must render whatever it is given. In `sparkles:syntax` an engine failure is reported before any event stream reaches a renderer, the caller then shows the plain source, and an unevaluable query pattern disables only itself; no degradation is sticky.

authority.text: Syntax highlighting survey: the highlighting problem

summary: A terminal grid cell stored in a few fixed bytes, with its code point and flattened style packed inline and only long graphemes kept out of line.
definition: The cell representation of the `sparkles:tui` frame grid: a packed code point plus a flat style, with graphemes too long to pack spilled to out-of-line storage, after the Notcurses and libvaxis inline packing. The render-core benchmark found that it lets a D renderer match a C one on the common workload.

summary: A terminal renderer that keeps the previous frame's cell grid and, for each new frame, writes only the runs of cells that changed.
definition: The `sparkles:tui` renderer: it retains the last rendered grid, compares the next one cell by cell, and emits one cursor move plus the styled text for each run of changed cells, so repainting a whole frame costs only its differences. Its retained grid reuses its storage, so a steady render loop allocates nothing.

summary: A Twoslash annotation drawn within a code line over the span it describes, such as a hover underline, a highlight box, or an error squiggle.
definition: The part of a Twoslash overlay that marks a span inside one line of code: hovers, highlights, and errors. The overlay planner sorts inline decorations so an enclosing span opens before a nested one; they never cross a line break.

summary: A Twoslash annotation rendered as extra rows beneath the code line it belongs to, such as an error message, a queried type, a completion list, or a tag line.
definition: The part of a Twoslash overlay that adds rows under a line of code: error messages, `^?` query results, completion lists, and `// @tag` lines. The overlay planner sorts them by line, and every backend flushes them at the line's end.

summary: A D struct annotated with option and argument attributes that both parses a command line into a value and renders a value back into the argument list of a tool to invoke.
definition: In `sparkles:dman`, the struct-with-UDAs model of a command: the same declaration parses `argv` into a struct for dman's own CLI and renders a struct into `argv` for third-party tools such as `git`, `jj` and `gh`, whose output a return-type-driven collector then decodes. Its option attributes are aliases over the `sparkles:wired` policy vocabulary, so one schema governs both the command line and JSON.

authority.text: dman command schema — three directions over one schema

summary: The complete token stream of a D source file, whitespace and comments included, that the D formatter lays out instead of a syntax tree.
definition: The sequence of tokens produced by DMD's lexer in its trivia configuration, which emits whitespace and comments as tokens, plus explicit entries for directives, a leading byte-order mark and the `__EOF__` tail. Concatenating the entries reproduces the input byte for byte, so the formatter can never lose text the way a tree-based printer can.

summary: Sorted arrays of syntax-node start positions that the D formatter queries by binary search instead of walking a syntax tree.
definition: The facts the formatter takes from DMD's parser: the start offsets of declarations, statements and expressions, collected in one parse-only pass and stored in sorted arrays. Layout consults them by binary search and never walks the tree; when the input does not parse, the oracle is empty and grouping falls back to bracket matching.

summary: The D formatter's set of transformations that add, remove or respell tokens, each with its own verifier and, except the trailing comma, off by default.
definition: The second of the formatter's two tiers. The layout tier changes only whitespace and is verified by token equality; a rewrite breaks token equality by construction, so each one ships with a verifier of its own and is opt-in, apart from trailing commas on broken lists. Rewrites whose safety needs resolved types are codemods, not part of this tier.

summary: The compiler identity a D analysis assumes, DMD, LDC, or LDC's GPU device compile, which fixes the predefined version identifiers, runtime sources and language rules applied to the code.
definition: A setting of a `sparkles:dmd-lsp` analysis that makes the DMD frontend see code as a particular compiler would: `dmd` (the default), `ldc`, or `ldcDevice` for the dcompute LDC's device compile of `@compute` shader modules. A `-mdcompute-targets=` flag selects `ldcDevice` on its own.

summary: A self-contained D snippet analyzed with no context beyond its own annotations and the compiler runtime's import path, as opposed to a file analyzed inside its dub project.
definition: The unit a Twoslash-style D analysis reads when no project is involved: one buffer whose only context is the runtime import path plus whatever its own `// @import:` and `// @dflags:` annotations declare. A file from a real project needs its dub project context instead, or every sibling import becomes an error.

summary: Choosing which repository files get documentation pages by following the links the documentation's Markdown makes, rather than walking the whole tree.
definition: The page-selection rule of `sparkles:docs`: a file gets a source-listing page only when the docs link to it, and a linked directory expands to its renderable subtree. The outcome, including every file skipped on purpose, is recorded in a manifest the site build reads instead of deciding again.

summary: An HTML output mode of the Sparkles UI toolkit in which a widget subtree carries no cell geometry, so the browser measures and wraps its text.
definition: A third HTML mode of `sparkles:ui`: a designated subtree emits semantic elements with class-based styling and no fixed cell widths, and composes with cell-grid subtrees on one page. It is the path by which documentation chrome becomes toolkit widgets without giving up proportional prose.
